narrative_purpose: Explains why a flattened blade beats a rope: an angled hydrofoil generates lift on the upstroke and the downstroke both, leaving an evenly spaced vortex chain instead of a churn.
subject: A broad flattened turquoise Na'vi tail shown at four successive moments of one complete up-and-down cycle, arranged left to right across a single stretch of clear water, the swimmer's lower back cropped at the left edge of each. In the first the blade is angled upward near the top of its sweep; in the second it is level and moving down fast; in the third it is angled downward near the bottom; in the fourth it is level again and rising. In every one of the four, a smooth continuous curved sheet of flow bends around the blade's surface rather than piling up behind it. Behind and below the whole sequence, a tidy chain of evenly spaced spiral eddies trails away to the right, alternating in rotation direction, each one about the same size.
scene: Clear mid-depth open seawater with fine suspended particles catching the light, no seabed and no other creatures.
camera: Straight-on side view of the whole four-phase sequence, all four tails at the same scale and depth.
light: Cool blue-green light from above raking across the wet blade surfaces, cyan highlights along the trailing edges, the spiral eddies faintly lit from within, deep indigo behind.
palette: Turquoise blade, ocean teal water, cyan flow highlights, void indigo depth.
style: Painterly naturalist motion study, organic and fluid, not an engineering schematic.
detail_level: High detail on each blade's angle and on the smooth sheet of flow bending around it; the eddy chain rendered as soft luminous spirals.
composition: Four phases spaced evenly across the middle band of the frame, the eddy chain running along the lower third, open darker water across the top for overlay callouts.
consistency_notes: The same tail four times through one cycle, not four different tails. The flow must read as a smooth bending sheet in every phase — never as a churn of bubbles, which is the opposite point. no artificial graphics: direction comes from the shape of the flow and the spacing of the eddies.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows or flow vectors, no engineering streamline diagram, no grid, no panel borders, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
